decisions.summary: P1 hook shape: bash with one python block on the review-round-hooks.sh model; the four fields joined with a unit separator because `read` collapses whitespace and the model field is usually empty.
decisions.why: Implementation mechanics for FR-001's refusal; the request names only a hook that rejects and a message, and this decides nothing about who is refused.

decisions.summary: P1 order of tests: non-Agent exits silently, then fork, then a non-empty model, then an agent file, else blocked/no-model.
decisions.why: Each branch is an FR the spec already settles (FR-001 pinned-type and model-named pass, FR-003 fork passes, FR-004's four slugs). The ORDER only decides which permit slug a fork carrying a model logs under, and both orders permit it.

decisions.summary: P1 an omitted subagent_type is read as general-purpose.
decisions.why: FR-001 names an omitted type among the ad-hoc set that is refused, and FR-004 requires the suite to cover it. Reading it as general-purpose refuses it.

decisions.summary: P1 root resolution for `.claude/agents/<type>.md`: clone-sync-hooks.sh resolve's clone, else the git top level of the payload's cwd, else the repository the hook lives in.
decisions.why: FR-001 gives the first two; the third is a last-resort fallback so a pinned type is still recognized when neither resolves, which serves FR-001's 'a dispatch of a type that HAS an agent file passes untouched' rather than cutting into the refusal.

decisions.summary: P1 a payload that is not JSON never blocks.
decisions.why: FR-001 refuses only when BOTH conditions are established from the payload - an ad-hoc subagent_type and no model. An unparseable payload establishes neither, so this is the rule being unevaluable, not an exception carved out of it. The measured failure (ad-hoc dispatches that named no model) arrives as harness JSON and is untouched.

decisions.summary: P3 an EMPTY model is refused, and a named model - `fable` included - passes.
decisions.why: An empty model is a dispatch that names none, so it runs on the session's model: refusing it is what the GM asked for ('the caller has to specify a model'). Passing any named model is FR-001 as written.

decisions.summary: P2 the rule text lives once in scripts/agent-model-rule.txt, read by the message; the suite asserts root CLAUDE.md carries the same two clauses.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires the guidance to be READ from one place the docs also state so a later change is made once; the plan picks that place and adds the drift assertion.

decisions.summary: P2 message composition: a bold first line naming the type and the session's model, the body from the rule file, then the script's name and the feature.
decisions.why: Consistent with FR-002 and SC-002, which still require all of the ordered content (the session's model and the 62-on-Fable measurement, the instruction to re-send with a model, and the sonnet/opus rule) to appear in the message the hook prints.

decisions.summary: P4 the hook is wired FIRST in the .claude/settings.json Agent matcher list, ahead of the pair, escalation and review-round guards.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks only that it be wired beside the other Agent-matched guards; position is free and refusing before the other guards act on a dispatch that will not run is inside that.

decisions.summary: P3/P4 suite scope (fixture repository with one agent file, every branch, the log records, the message, the unknown mode, a Bash call), the firing-log payload row, the CLAUDE.md and docs/guards.md rows, no new make target.
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for exactly these; the unknown-mode case and the Bash case are coverage of the guard's own entry points, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Order T01 hook+rule file+suite, T02 wiring+log row+record, T03 make hooks-test, make quick, prove it fires by deleting the refusal branch, land; route DIRECT; no escape token added.
decisions.why: SC-003 asks for the green suites and the delete-the-branch proof; FR-004 says there is no escape token; the spec states the DIRECT route.
